content.content:
=== later.py
later.py: his messages after an entry's creation that may bear on it, though no commit of the
entry followed them (his later word may have gone into a skill or another record instead).

    python3 -I later.py 148                   (or P-148)
    python3 -I later.py 148 --top 25          how many to print (default 15)
    python3 -I later.py 148 --at 36f7db77c --until 2026-10-21T20:54
                                              the entry's text at a commit, and no message after a time

The candidates are his messages in the coordinating sessions (tlib.COORDINATING) from the entry's
creation on (for an entry struck from POSITIONS.md, its last text is read, and the list runs on
past the removal) (the first commit of its trail that made its text), less those that leads.py already
printed near the entry's own commits. Each is scored by the entry's distinctive terms:
  - its title's words, beyond common words (a stop list, and words in more than a tenth of his
    messages), lightly stemmed (possessive and plural off, cut to 7 letters); each weighs its
    rarity in his messages, log(messages / messages holding it);
  - its names in backticks, weight 3 each.
A term in his own words (lines that do not start with ">") counts whole; a term only in the
exchange around his message (the coordinator's message he answered, by the reply chain, its
reply to him, and the lines he quoted) counts half. A message also gains 8 when it falls in the
30 minutes before a commit that changed a file the entry names in backticks (`compiler.md`), other
than the entry's own commits, in lines that hold a title term (3 when the lines hold none): that
is where his word may have gone. Naming the entry's number (P-148, or as dictated, P148) adds 8 in
his words, 2 in the exchange. A message is a candidate when its weight is at least 5 (MIN) and it
holds a term in his own words or falls before such a commit. Printed: rank, weight, time, whether it
is after the entry's last change, the terms (in parentheses when only in the exchange), the commit
it precedes, and its first 300 characters; then how many candidates there were in all.

=== near.py
near.py: the curator's messages in a window before a UTC time, each with the coordinating
session's message that it answered, found along the transcript's reply chain.

    python3 -I near.py 2026-09-26T10:22:23Z            window 60 minutes before the time
    python3 -I near.py 2026-09-26T10:22:23Z 15m        or 2h, 1d
    python3 -I near.py 2026-09-26T10:22:23Z 15m --cut 2000
                                                        cut each printed text at 2000 characters
                                                        (his and the coordinator's), saying so;
                                                        by default every text is printed whole

For each message of his: its time, source (main, s1, queued: see show.py), session, length and
full text. Then the message he answered: the coordinator's turn that his message follows on the
reply chain (tlib.py says how the chain is read), every text of that turn whole, each with its
time and the file and line it was read from (the first copy, when a resumed transcript replays
it). Before it, one line for each turn the chain passed over as not addressed to him (replies to
Stop-hook feedback, to an agent's message or hand-back, to a task notification or check-in, to a
system reminder), and for each text written after he sent his message; a passed-over turn that
answers a notification and ends with an ask to him (a question mark, "The ask", "I recommend",
"your yes", ...) is marked, and the newest such turn printed whole, since he may have answered
it. When he quotes lines ("> ..."), the text on the chain that holds them is named, and printed
whole if it is not the answer. After it, the last lines of the three turns to him further back
on the chain, for a message that answers an older question. A queued message (sent while a turn
ran) starts at its delivery into the turn; texts written after he sent it are not taken. A
message on no chain the index holds (a queued one never delivered) falls back to the time: the
coordinator's last text before it, passing over replies to Stop-hook feedback.

=== quote.py
quote.py: does the curator's message at a UTC time hold a quote word for word?

    python3 -I quote.py "QUOTE" 2026-09-26T10:21:32Z
    python3 -I quote.py "QUOTE" 2026-09-26T10:21        a prefix: every message of his in that minute

The time is a prefix of his message's timestamp, as show.py takes it (a trailing Z is dropped).
For each message of his at that time it prints one verdict:
  EXACT        the quote is a substring of the message as stored
  NORMALISED   a substring once both have every run of whitespace made one space, ends trimmed,
               and the curly apostrophe U+2019 made a straight one (nothing else is changed)
  NO MATCH     neither; it then prints the longest run of the quote's words that the
               message holds word for word (after the same normalising), for a reader to judge
With the match it prints the message's text around it.

=== trail.py
trail.py: the trail of one entry of POSITIONS.md, from the repository's history.

    python3 -I trail.py 86            (or P-86)
    python3 -I trail.py 86 --short    the commit list only, one line each
    python3 -I trail.py 86 --at REV   the record as commit REV holds it

Prints:
  1. the entry's text at HEAD (for an entry struck from POSITIONS.md: STRUCK at the top, with the
     commit that removed it and the reason its history block gives, and the text as it last stood);
  2. its blocks in POSITIONS-history.md at HEAD, each with the commit that wrote it (the oldest
     commit whose history file holds the block's provenance line). A block's own "commit X" names
     the source it cites, not its writer;
  3. every commit that made or changed the entry's text, oldest first, read from each commit's own
     tree (side branches included): hash, UTC author time, subject, what it did, how the link to
     the text before was made (number, line, title: exact; similarity: score printed), how many
     other entries of POSITIONS.md the commit changed, and the reasons on record: the history
     blocks it wrote, the comments above verbatim copies of the text in the old history file, and
     the commit message.
  4. a cross-check: the old history lines that the numbering block names as earlier texts of this
     entry, and whether each is a text of this trail.

What a commit did:
  created          a text new in POSITIONS.md that no removed or earlier text explains
  changed          a text that replaced another of the same commit (link: number, line, title or similarity)
  moved to history the text left POSITIONS.md and stands verbatim in POSITIONS-history.md
  archived         a verbatim copy stored in POSITIONS-history.md by a later commit
  re-created       a text new in POSITIONS.md made from an earlier text (archived or removed)
  restored         a text back in POSITIONS.md verbatim from POSITIONS-history.md
  renumbered       the same text under a new number (2026-10-13: none -> P-n)
  struck           the number left POSITIONS.md (the first event of a struck entry's trail)
=== pointers.py
pointers.py: every line of the record that names an entry of POSITIONS.md by its number.

    python3 -I pointers.py 86            (or P-86)
    python3 -I pointers.py 86 --at REV   the files as commit REV holds them

Searches, at the working tree: explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md, POSITIONS.md, PLAN.md,
review-queue.md, HELD.md and BOOT.md; explorations/reviews/open-asks-*.md; and every file under
.claude/skills/. The history files (POSITIONS-history.md, FACTS-history.md) are not searched:
trail.py reads the first, and both only record. A line counts when it holds the number as a word:
P-86 matches, as in "P-86's" or "(P-86)", but P-860 and P-186 do not. A line that names a range
holding the number ("P-85 to P-88") is listed too, marked as a range.
Prints path:line and the line (cut at 400 characters around the number; --whole prints it whole),
grouped by file; the entry's own line in POSITIONS.md is marked.

=== homes.py
homes.py: where a status that an entry of POSITIONS.md states may already live.

    python3 -I homes.py 151            (or P-151)
    python3 -I homes.py 151 --top 8    candidates per sentence (default 5)
    python3 -I homes.py 151 --at REV   the three files as commit REV holds them

Splits the entry (the working tree's POSITIONS.md; for an entry struck from it, its text as it
last stood, said so at the top) into sentences, and a sentence into its clauses
at the semicolons outside parentheses; a clause keeps the label that opens its sentence, as
"Built:" or "Still to build:". A clause states a status when it, its label or its sentence holds
one of the status words: built, to build, landed, pending, default, waits, standing go, listed for his
review, open, held, parked, owed, taken, stands at, returns after, not moved, and the like.

For each such clause it lists the candidates that may already hold the same point: the numbered
items of review-queue.md's lists (b) and (c), and the lines of PLAN.md (a numbered sub-line also
carries its parent's item number, and its own number as a fork when the parent counts forks).
A candidate is listed when it names the entry or shares a distinctive term with the clause:
  row N, item N (PLAN's), review-queue item N, fork N, way N, batch N, rung X, phase N, ask N,
  decision X, another entry's P-N, a name in backticks (a commit hash too), a dotted finding
  name such as judge-review.1 or A.skeptic.2
Each shared term weighs by its rarity among the candidates (log of the candidates over those
holding it); naming the entry adds 2; content words shared (four letters or more, beyond common
words) add a little, to order near-ties, and are printed apart. Candidates are ranked by that
weight, and each is printed with what it shares, for the scout to confirm or reject.

=== comments.py
comments.py: his saved page comments that bear on an entry of POSITIONS.md.

    python3 -I comments.py 66            (or P-66)

He also comments on pages, and those comments are not in the transcripts. They are saved as
explorations/coordinator/positions-audit/evidence/curator-comments-*.md: a section per thread,
headed "## On <what it was anchored to>", with one bullet per comment, "- HH:MM: "words"".
A section counts when its heading, or a comment counts when its own words, either
  - name the entry's number, also as dictated: P-66, P66, PE66, P 66 (not P-660), or
  - quote its title: a quoted run ("..." or curly quotes) of at least three content words, at
    least 60 % of which are words of the entry's bold title (case, possessives and punctuation
    ignored).
A section that counts is printed whole, with its heading; a comment that counts in another
section is printed with that section's heading. Each with its file and line.

=== hischeck.py
hischeck.py: check the block of his quotes that a scout's or reader's report ends with.

    python3 -I hischeck.py FILE...

Each FILE holds a block headed "## His quotes" (to the next "## " heading or the end), one line
per quote of his:
    HIS 2026-09-26T10:21:32.097Z | Run Fable judgement as well.
(a line may be wrapped in backticks or start with "- "). The time is a prefix of his message's
timestamp, as show.py takes it (a trailing Z dropped); each message of his at that time is tried,
and the quote is checked as quote.py does:
  EXACT        a substring of the message as stored
  NORMALISED   a substring once whitespace is collapsed and U+2019 made a straight apostrophe
  NO MATCH     neither, in every message at that time (quote.py "QUOTE" TIME shows the nearest run)
  NO MESSAGE   no message of his at that time
Lines of the block that start with HIS but do not parse are counted as BAD FORM. Prints, per
file, the counts and every line that is not EXACT or NORMALISED, with its line number; exits 1
when any line fails or a file has no block.

# Where this repository's history comes from

## The facts

- `palimondo/fortress` is a GitHub fork, created 2018-05-10, of `sirinath/fortress` (GitHub API: `fork: true`, `parent` and `source` both `sirinath/fortress`). That repository is a git conversion of the project's java.net Mercurial repository (it carries a `refs/import/*` namespace; the conversion mechanism is inferred, not verified). Its `master` is `a874948ac`; its relic branches and its `1.0` tag (`0e8ede7e7`) match this repository's `origin/*` refs exactly. Nobody in the tree or the transcripts had named sirinath before this note.
- The trunk: `git rev-list --count a874948ac` = 5,397; with the twelve relic branches 5,558. The true root is `72ae6881b` (jm143038, 2007-01-04); the trunk tip `a874948ac` (karl.naden, 2012-08-31). The conversion cut 146 parent links, so `a874948ac` has 147 parentless roots and a first-parent walk from the tip stops after six commits at `5a68404fd` (2012-07-19); `research/authorship.md:14-22`, corrected in `6beb45ec7`. Pavol has no commits between 2013 and 2026.
- The third-party port: `pluckyporcupine/fortress` is exactly one commit, `eab48aa6d` ("Initial commit.", author field "Matt Chelen", 2018-10-11), a squash based on a June 2012 tree, `build.xml` at Scala 2.10.7 and Java source level 1.9, README saying compiled programs do not run. It shares no git history with this repository.
- The graft: `8fe1daa8f` (2026-08-18, session 01LjDz79) copied 1,506 of that commit's files onto `a874948ac` (1,493 added, 13 modified); `c353a7676` regenerated the AST sources. One graft commit, not several. The instruction came from the HANDOVER.md of an earlier chat session (redacted in the archive; the compaction summary of 2026-08-19 01:58 records the prescription).
- What became of it: the old Scala jars removed in `439604f53`; the port's README replaced in `b7f53317d`; its scratch files and `NOTES.md` removed in `bbd34ca2a`; the vendored BCEL (388 files) removed in `f7c4bf0f2`. The spike `73f598202` (`spike/scala-upgrade`) showed the build revives on JDK 8 with five files and nothing from the port. Branch `clean-ladder` (14 commits, tip `8332bd34f`, revival commit `f39bee468`) was rebuilt directly on `a874948ac` with no graft.
- The rebuild never replaced `main`: `origin/main` still descends from `8fe1daa8f`; `git merge-base main origin/clean-ladder` is `a874948ac`. Pavol's plan to rename `clean-ladder` to `main` (transcript, 2026-08-23 19:13) is recorded nowhere as done. What the graft still leaves in `main`'s tree, by blob comparison: 6 of its 13 modified files byte-identical to the graft's version (`FTypeTuple`, `NodeFactory`, `InstrumentedParserGenerator`, `Util`, `ParserMaker`, `RatsUtil`) and 72 of its 1,493 added files (63 generated `nodes/` files, `Library/FortressAst.fsi`/`.fss`, two `contrib/Atom/language-fortress` files, the ant 1.9.10 jars, `default_repository/caches/global.map`, untracked since 2026-10-04, see the verdict); 406 added files are gone and 1,015 have changed since.

## Pavol's words (transcript `bdff267d`, part 000, `transcripts` branch)

- 2026-08-22 00:17: "Is this caused by us starting the modernization from porcupine's repo on top of our original? … That would be an argument to base the clean modernization ladder from original repo fork and just apply the changes which make it work, instead of doing the 'graft' from porcupine's repo."
- 2026-08-23 04:40: "I don't think we need to credit them if we are rewriting it, basically, from scratch using few mechanical fixes. So maybe we can lose the porcupines credit since you seem to have not really been informed by their changes."
- 2026-08-23 14:17: "We are in a gradual process of removing all mentions of [the] migration. Only benefit from that one was we [learned] it was possible to do the migration … the rest was all about removing mistakes that they did during their migration. So I don't wanna see them mentioned anywhere."
- 2026-08-23 19:13: "I believe this concludes our clean [ladder] more or less. I still will need to rename … the main branch to that one."

## The wrong sentence

`CLAUDE.md`'s opening paragraph, written in `446836590` (2026-08-19) and never changed until `2026-09-23`, said the repository "carries the full available git history … with pluckyporcupine's Scala 2.10.7/Java 9 migration grafted on top as a tree overlay". The versions were right; the sentence omitted the fork's source, presented the toolchain as the port's migration when the working toolchain owes it nothing, and contradicted the decision of 2026-08-23. Corrected on Pavol's instruction.

## Files that still repeat it, for the cleaner pass or for a decision

`README.md:227-231` (the Subversion story, no fork step); `research/authorship.md:16-18, 207-214` ("the GitHub mirror" unnamed; "tree overlay"); `explorations/repo-internals.md:90-92` (says the graft "rewrote directories wholesale"; false, the cut links are the conversion's), `:161`, `:241`; `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-rr64-functions/round-history.md:8` ("parentless import roots from the graft"; false); `explorations/test-baseline-jdk8.md:3-4, 101`; `explorations/coordinator/INDEX.md:37`; `explorations/coordinator/oracle-headers.md:47`; `explorations/modernization-plan.md:73, 232-234`; `explorations/readme-plan.md:9-10, 64-69` (says the clean-ladder rebuild still starts from the graft; superseded by the spike); `explorations/process-audit.md:368`; `research/extracts/SteeleJuliaCon2016-extract.md:192`; `explorations/rebuild-plan.md:11, 338` and `explorations/c2-proposal.md` (plans that describe the replacement as history).

## Verification against Pavol's recollection (the same worker, re-briefed)

Pavol's recollection: main restarted from the sirinath copy and redid the modernization cleanly; nothing from the port should be on main. Checked:

- History: `8fe1daa8f` is an ancestor of `origin/main` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`); `origin/clean-ladder` (`8332bd34f`) is not; their merge base is `a874948ac`. After his "I still will need to rename the main branch to that one" (transcript bdff267d part 000, 2026-08-23 19:13) and the coordinator's "tomorrow you run the tag script and rename the branch" (19:13), the same session went on committing on `claude/handover-reading-vn8zgr` and pushing it to `main` from 22:05 on, through the microGPT work. No transcript records a rename, merge or cherry-pick of `clean-ladder`; no `modernization/*` tag was pushed until 2026-10-02, when Pavol pushed them from his machine, annotated, on the existing commits, with the messages approved in `c2-proposal.md` § 3 (`modernization/jdk8-baseline` `002e997b8`, `modernization/scala-2.12` `5c1e40047`, `modernization/jdk11`, `jdk17` and `jdk21` `69b01f695`, `modernization/asm-9` `2de75c02a`, `modernization/scala-2.13` `c4a10003d` and `modernization/jdk25` `8332bd34f`); `clean-ladder` was not renamed. One run did start from `clean-ladder`: `codex/astra-microgpt` (`explorations/astra/README.md:3`), whose documents alone came into main. So main continued the grafted line; the clean restart exists only as the unmerged branch.
- Working code: of the 78 byte-identical blobs, 4 are identical in `clean-ladder` too (the `import xtc.parser.Module` disambiguation in four parser files, made independently in `69b01f695`), nothing owed. 74 exist because of the graft: 63 generated `nodes/` files, `Operators.java`, `Library/FortressAst.fsi`/`.fss` (build output the 2012 trunk did not commit and `clean-ladder`'s `.gitignore:77-84` ignores; main tracks all 1,071 `nodes/` files); `FTypeArrayList.java` plus two lines in `FTypeTuple.java`, the port's fix for the JDK 8 `TreeSet` `ClassCastException`, whose `compareTo` always returns 0, harmless because both sets get one element, and **the only piece of the port main's code runs** (`clean-ladder` fixes the same bug with `listComparer`, `f39bee468`); cosmetic edits in `NodeFactory.java`; the unused ant 1.9.10 jars; the unused `contrib/Atom/language-fortress/`; the tracked `global.map`, an empty linker map of four zero bytes (untracked since 2026-10-04). Graft lines inside files edited later: `build.xml` (a dead `checkEnv` 1.9 condition, a dead `scala-lib` classpath entry), seven `@Deprecated` in `NamingCzar.java`, three `case e:Throwable` in `STypeChecker.scala` (same behaviour), one `.gitignore` comment.
- Everything else main differs from `clean-ladder` in (1,232 files) is the tracked `nodes/`, the revival's tests and library, compiler, runtime and checker edits after `sealed-tree`, the `experiment/` briefs, and the launcher scripts main's own rungs edited.

Verdict: on history the recollection is wrong, on working code largely right. Removable with no behaviour change, for the cleaner pass: the `FTypeArrayList` fix replaced by `clean-ladder`'s two lines, the dead jars, the Atom package, `global.map` (ported 2026-10-04: untracked, and ignored by `clean-ladder`'s `.gitignore` line; `clean-ladder` adds no code for it, because the 2012 linker writes the empty map wherever it is missing, `linker/RepoState.java:366-385`, on both paths; checked with no restore by a build, the library order, a compiled run and both suites), the dead `build.xml` lines, the cosmetic edits; untracking the generated sources changes the workflow CLAUDE.md describes (stale-AST regeneration, committed determinism). Main's history contains `8fe1daa8f` unless main is replaced by or rebased onto `clean-ladder`.

content.content:
Print the curator's message(s) at a UTC timestamp or its prefix, verbatim.

    python3 -I show.py 2026-10-12T15:53          # every message of his in that minute
    python3 -I show.py 2026-10-12T15:53:07.5     # a finer prefix
    python3 -I show.py --list 2026-10-12         # one line per message (timestamp, source, length, start)
    python3 -I show.py --count                   # how many messages the three sources give

A prefix may use a space instead of the T and may end in Z. All times are UTC.

His messages come from three places, and the header of each printed message says which:
  main  the main-session lines of the transcripts in /root/.claude/projects/-home-user-fortress/
        and /home/user/fortress-transcripts-blinded/projects/-home-user-fortress/ (the .parts
        folders included): `user` lines that are not isMeta, not sidechain, with text content
        that does not start with '<' and is not a compaction summary; deduplicated by uuid,
        because a resumed transcript replays earlier lines.
  s1    the same lines of the first coordinating session (bdff267d), read with `git show` from
        the `transcripts` branch (origin/transcripts) of this repository, 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-17.
        Skipped, with a note on stderr, if that branch is not in the clone.
  queued  a message he queued while an agent was busy that no `user` line holds as its text
        (the queue-operation `enqueue` lines and the queued_command attachments); its time is the
        time he sent it.
Nothing is filtered by author or by kind: a scheduled check-in or a pasted report that arrived as a
`user` line is printed too, so a reader decides what is his.

The question is whether one object may belong to two members of the family at once, say `Tag[String]` and `Tag[ZZ32]`. The designers called forbidding that "multiple instantiation exclusion". It matters because of generic functions: call `pick[X](t: Tag[X])` on such an object and `X` has two answers. A checker that assumes one answer can pick the wrong one and generate code that fails at run time. That is the six-line program the rung found.

**What each path does today.** The compiled checker forbids the double membership, and its return-type check relies on there being one answer. The interpreter allows it, and when it must choose it takes whichever instantiation the object lists first, so swapping the order of an extends clause changes the result, and a differently shaped program dies at run time there too. Both paths have a hole; they are different holes.

**What the spec says.** It allows a type to extend two instantiations, with a worked example. It forbids two overloads of one name whose static parameters differ, which is the same sentence behind the 35 errors in the triage. And it fixes the static arguments at the call site. So the spec is stricter than both paths on overloads and sides with the interpreter on the double membership.

**Where it bites the tower.** Exactly there. `ZZ32` extends `ZZ64`, and each is an `Equality` of itself, an `Integral` of itself, an ordering of itself. def indexes():
    global _INDEX
    if _INDEX is None:
        _INDEX = [_cached(name, key, fn) for src, name, key, fn in _files()]
    return _INDEX


def load_msgs():
    """show.load()'s list, from the cached indexes: dicts with ts, source, sid, text (and uuid, or
    qh for a queued message)."""
    seen, queued = {}, {}
    for idx in indexes():
        for k, key, rec in idx['msgs']:
            if k == 'h':
                seen.setdefault(key, rec)
            else:
                queued.setdefault(key, rec)
    msgs = list(seen.values())
    blob = ' '.join(show._norm(m['text']) for m in msgs)
    for n, m in queued.items():
        if n not in blob:
            msgs.append(m)
    msgs.sort(key=lambda m: (m['ts'], m['source']))
    return msgs


class Node:
    __slots__ = ('uuid', 'parent', 'kind', 'label', 'ts', 'sid', 'where', 'text')

    def __init__(self, t, where):
        self.uuid, self.parent, self.kind, self.label, self.ts, self.sid, line, self.text = t
        self.where = '%s:%d' % (short_path(where), line)


class Talk:
    def __init__(self):
        self.msgs = load_msgs()
        self.nodes, self.alias, self.hisq, self.enq = {}, {}, {}, {}
        for idx in indexes():
            w = idx['where']
            for t in idx['nodes']:
                if t[0] not in self.nodes:
                    nd = Node(t, w)
                    self.nodes[t[0]] = nd
                    if nd.kind == 'hisq':
                        self.hisq.setdefault((nd.sid, nd.label), nd)
            for u, p in idx['alias'].items():
                self.alias.setdefault(u, p)
            for sid, ts, h in idx['enq']:
                self.enq.setdefault((sid, h), []).append(ts)
        self.by_sid = {}
        for nd in self.nodes.values():
            if nd.kind == 'text':
                self.by_sid.setdefault(nd.sid, []).append(nd)
        for v in self.by_sid.values():
            v.sort(key=lambda x: x.ts)
        self.keys = {s: [x.ts for x in v] for s, v in self.by_sid.items()}
